questions.question: Describe the problem scenario that starts Term 1 and explain why ordinary hand tools cannot solve it.
questions.expected_answer: People are trapped in a vehicle whose body has been crushed and folded in a collision, so doors and roof pillars cannot be opened by hand. Hand tools fail because folded steel is too strong for human muscles, hammers would shake and injure the trapped person, saws are slow and cause dangerous vibration, and flame cutting is unsafe near leaking fuel. The need is a tool that produces a very large but slow, controlled force.

questions.question: Explain how the Jaws of Life produces its force, naming the two technological systems it combines.
questions.expected_answer: A pump driven by an engine or motor pushes oil along a hose into a cylinder in the tool; the oil presses on a wide piston, and because liquid cannot be compressed, a small pump produces a very large push. This is a hydraulic system. The arms of the spreader or blades of the cutter are levers, which multiply the force again. So the tool combines hydraulics and levers.

questions.question: Write a one-sentence problem statement for the scenario and list four requirements any solution must meet.
questions.expected_answer: Problem statement: people trapped in crushed vehicles need to be freed quickly, safely and without further injury using a tool that gives a large, controlled force. Requirements, any four: strong enough to bend or cut steel; portable; controllable so it moves a little at a time; safe, with no sparks or flame near fuel; works in rain and darkness; does not injure the trapped person.
